signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hike Speculation
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records an extreme weekly bilateral divergence, with JPY leading at +2.414% across 7 pairs while NZD lags at -1.406% across 4 pairs, generating a wide 3.819% spread. JPY strengthens despite a nominal carry deficit against NZD, where RBNZ sits at 2.75% against BoJ at 1.0% with a +175bp NZD advantage. Fresh headlines showing yen advances on BoJ rate hike speculation accelerate the move, while NZD COT positioning reflects deeply stretched short exposure with leveraged funds net short -32,496 contracts at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (z -2.60). Technically, NZD/USD trades below its SMA20 of 0.5911, leaving NZD cross downside exposed as JPY capital repatriation continues. Trade bias: Short NZD/JPY; cross-asset momentum overrides the nominal carry disadvantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ leaves policy stance unchanged and dampens hike speculation, triggering an aggressive unwind of fresh JPY longs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.05, breaking down through its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 159.04, 160.59, and 158.45. Options pricing reflects an extreme asymmetric downside bias with 1M 25d risk reversals printing at -2.54, even while the Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% differential maintains a +275bp USD carry cushion (SOFR-TONA spread at +267bp). Leveraged funds remain net short JPY at -81,619 contracts (9th percentile, z -1.34), leaving substantial room for short-covering flows if support gives way. The implied volatility of 7.2% against realized HV30 of 10.2% produces a negative vol risk premium of -3.0%, indicating thin options protection against further spot drops despite the sharp downside put skew. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe risk reversal put demand and positioning vulnerability override carry support. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: US economic data extensions push US 10Y yields above 4.85%, reinstating dollar carry demand.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Vol + Retail
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7207, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster anchored by the SMA20 at 0.7129. Leveraged funds hold a crowded net long position of +53,578 contracts, situated in the 95th percentile of its 52-week distribution (z +1.92). In direct contrast, retail sentiment registers an extreme 90% short bias, setting up a severe institutional-versus-retail divergence. The RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% policy spread grants AUD a 60bp carry advantage, backed by a -70bp SOFR vs AONIA differential. With ATM implied volatility at 7.2% against HV30 of 6.1% reflecting a mild +1.0% premium, the market is pricing stable continuation rather than sudden reversal risk. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning and carry advantage dominate retail fading. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger profit-taking if spot drops through the SMA20 support at 0.7129.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Capitulation + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1621, positioned between its SMA20 at 1.1609 and the SMA200 resistance at 1.1637. CFTC data shows aggressive leveraged fund selling, with net exposure dropping by -55,635 contracts week-on-week to -55,311 contracts, collapsing to the 3rd percentile of its 52-week range (z -2.28). Options markets indicate defensive positioning, with 1M implied volatility at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.6%, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.5%. The Fed at 3.75% vs ECB at 2.4% maintains a 135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, reinforced by a +146bp SOFR-€STR OIS spread. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; aggressive institutional short additions and carry headwind restrict upside momentum. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep. Risk: ECB delivers a hawkish hike signal, forcing rapid covering of crowded speculative short contracts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Positioning Crowding
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3516, resting below its SMA20 of 1.3554 but holding above the SMA50/200 support zone at 1.3449/1.3446. Leveraged funds hold an extended net long position of +56,839 contracts, standing at the 96th percentile of its 52-week range (z +1.58) following a +10,769 contract weekly build. Options markets exhibit heavy event protection demand, with 1M implied volatility printing at 11.0% against HV30 of 4.7%, driving an extreme vol risk premium of +6.3%. With BoE at 3.75% vs Fed at 3.75% offering neutral policy rate carry and a negligible -8bp SONIA-SOFR spread, currency direction depends on data execution. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; crowded long positioning and elevated hedging costs warn of consolidation. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: Spot closes below the SMA200 at 1.3446, invalidating the broader upward trend structure.
